A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Harpoon research work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–I, including equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original imputation and constrained-generation experiments, empirical gradient measurements, ablations and runtime results in Section 4 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The training objective, dirty-estimate definition in Eq. 3, sampling algorithm and inference losses remain unchanged. The Appendix B correction concerns a proof expression, not the method specified in Algorithm 1 and Appendices D/H.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight datasets, MAR/MCAR/MNAR imputation scenarios, and range, categorical, conjunctive and disjunctive constraints. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Imputation comparisons retain GAIN, MIRACLE, GReaT, Remasker and DiffPuter; constraint-generation comparisons retain DiffPuter and GReaT. The newly cited Scassola et al. method is not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The 70/30 train-test splits, missingness ratios, preprocessing, constraint specifications and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix G also retains the same backbone, 200 diffusion steps, 1000 training epochs and guidance settings.

E4.justification: The gradient-angle analysis in Figure 3, loss and guidance-schedule ablations in Tables 4–5, and encoding/preprocessing analyses in Tables 14–16 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report fixed random seeds, five independent trials, and means with standard deviations. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and empirical findings are unchanged throughout the main text and Appendix I. For example, Table 1 retains Harpoon's Adult MAR imputation MSE of 0.99 with standard deviation 0.08 at 25% missingness.

T1.justification: Appendix B, p. 17, corrects swapped square-root factors in the final substitution for Q_t in Theorem 3.1's proof. v3 uses sqrt(alpha_bar_t) as the denominator and sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t) multiplying the noise estimate, restoring consistency with Eq. 3. The assumptions and theorem statements are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the algorithm contribution from 'the first manifold-aware conditional tabular diffusion method' to 'a manifold-aware conditional tabular diffusion method,' narrowing the priority claim. The theoretical-priority claim, abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The manifold-based mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental results, disjunction-related tradeoffs and limitations of continuous diffusion remain unchanged. Section 3.2's revised distinction from prior methods retains the existing emphasis on theoretical justification.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware/software information, data-processing instructions and code/data access disclosures are unchanged, including Appendices C and E–H.

R1.justification: v3 adds Scassola et al. (2025), 'Zero-shot conditioning of score-based diffusion models by neuro-symbolic constraints.' Sections 2 and 3.2 acknowledge its training-free tabular guidance and distinguish Harpoon through geometric justification and the class of theoretically supported objectives.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the contribution bullet, related-work discussion and theoretical-positioning paragraph. The acknowledgements add Dutch Research Council support. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Local reflow adjusts heading spacing, shifts Figure 1 slightly within page 3 and compresses bibliography spacing around the added reference. Figures and tables retain their content, captions and design.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes an algebraic inconsistency in Appendix B and improves attribution and novelty framing by acknowledging Scassola et al. and removing the algorithmic 'first' claim. These provide limited gains in mathematical consistency and research positioning; the method, experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
